overview.title: What is Sealand?
overview.text: Sealand is a self-declared micronation on a former WWII sea fort in the North Sea, seven miles off England's eastern coast, claiming independence since 1967.

overview.title: Who joins Sealand?
overview.text: Sealand's community spans 105+ countries. Members are drawn by the principality's founding story and the chance to hold a genuine title of nobility from a self-declared sovereign state. Sealand offers noble titles ranging from Lord and Lady up to Duke and Duchess, as well as an e-citizenship program that extends digital membership worldwide.

overview.title: Sealand's national motto and mission
overview.text: Sealand's motto is "E Mare Libertas" (From the Sea, Freedom). Revenue from title sales funds upkeep of the platform and a growing sports program with 300+ athletes across nine national teams. The principality is run by the Bates family, a hereditary monarchy founded by Prince Roy and now led by Sovereign Prince Michael.

history.text:
Sealand was founded on September 2, 1967, when Paddy Roy Bates - a British pirate radio broadcaster - occupied HM Fort Roughs, a decommissioned WWII anti-aircraft sea fort 11 km off the coast of Suffolk, England. Bates declared independence and named himself Prince Roy of Sealand.

The principality's claim to sovereignty rests in part on a 1968 British court ruling that found it had no jurisdiction over the platform, which at the time lay outside the UK's three-nautical-mile territorial limit. A constitution was adopted in 1975, formalizing Sealand's flag, anthem, currency, and passport system.

Sealand survived a dramatic 1978 coup attempt in which German and Dutch mercenaries seized the platform while the Bates family was lured abroad. Prince Roy retook Sealand by helicopter assault and held the ringleaders as prisoners of war until Germany sent a diplomat from its London embassy to negotiate their release - an act the Bates family has since cited as evidence of tacit recognition.

Prince Roy died in October 2012, and his son Prince Michael assumed the full title of Sovereign Prince. Today the principality funds itself through noble title sales, e-citizenship subscriptions, and collectibles.

location:
Sealand sits on HM Fort Roughs, a WWII-era sea fort at coordinates 51 degrees 53' 40" N, 01 degrees 28' 57" E - roughly 11 km (7 miles) from the Suffolk coast in the North Sea. The structure is a 4,500-ton reinforced concrete and steel platform with a deck approximately 60 feet (18 m) above sea level, boarded via a manual crane-operated swing rather than any stairs or ladder from water level.

The inhabitable area is approximately 550 m2 (5,920 sq. ft.) - roughly the length of two tennis courts. The interior includes bedrooms, a national cathedral, and historical server rooms from the HavenCo internet hosting venture of the early 2000s. Power comes from solar panels and wind turbines; fresh water is collected rainwater.

Physical visits are currently suspended. The official site notes that Sealand is actively evaluating the situation and that trips may become available again in the future, with priority access for e-citizens.
duration:
Noble titles from Sealand are permanent and hereditary - purchased once and carried for life, with the right to pass them down. There is no expiry or renewal fee for the title itself.

Sealand e-citizenship is a rolling monthly subscription at $9.99/month, cancellable at any time. The optional physical e-citizen ID card is a separate one-time purchase.

Sealand has no residential program. As of August 2024, the platform has one permanent resident: Mike Barrington, the engineer and caretaker. The Bates royal family lives primarily in Southend-on-Sea, Essex.

howToEnter.text:
To join Sealand, [purchase a noble title](https://sealandgov.org/en-us/collections/titles) from the official store. Titles range from Lord/Lady ($29.99) to Duke/Duchess ($749.99) and are permanent and hereditary once issued. Lower tiers (Lord/Lady, Baron/Baroness) are delivered digitally; Count/Countess and Duke/Duchess include a luxury parchment deed signed by Sovereign Prince Michael and shipped within 5-10 business days.

For e-citizenship, visit the [e-citizenship page](https://sealandgov.org/en-us/pages/sealand-e-citizenship) and subscribe at $9.99/month. E-citizenship is independent of noble titles and can be held separately. Availability has fluctuated - the program closed at end of 2024 and reopened; always confirm current status on the official site before purchasing.

Physical residency is not available. Visits to the platform are currently suspended.

faqs.question: Is Sealand a real country?
faqs.answer: Sealand is not recognized by any sovereign state under mainstream international law. However, it has operated continuously since 1967 with its own flag, constitution, currency, and government. A 1968 British court ruling found it had no jurisdiction over the platform, which the Bates family cites as de facto recognition. The UK's position since 1987, when it extended territorial waters to 12 miles, is that Sealand falls within British jurisdiction - a point Sealand disputes.

faqs.question: What does a Sealand noble title actually include?
faqs.answer: Sealand noble titles are permanent and hereditary. Lord/Lady and Baron/Baroness tiers include a digital deed you can print at home. Count/Countess and Duke/Duchess include a luxury parchment deed with an embossed gold coat of arms, personally signed by Sovereign Prince Michael. The Knighthood (Sir/Dame) makes you a member of the Sovereign Military Order of Sealand. The official site is transparent: "there aren't any outright noble privileges you can gain," but title-holders can style themselves with the title on personal correspondence and documentation.

faqs.question: Can you live on Sealand?
faqs.answer: Physical residency is not offered as a program. As of August 2024, Sealand has one permanent resident: Mike Barrington, the engineer who serves as caretaker and head of homeland security. The royal family lives primarily in Southend-on-Sea, Essex. The inhabitable deck area is roughly 550 m2 (about the size of two tennis courts). See the official blog post [Can you live on Sealand?](https://sealandgov.org/en-us/blogs/news/can-you-live-on-sealand) for more.

faqs.question: Can you visit Sealand?
faqs.answer: Visits are currently suspended. The official site states that trips have been temporarily paused while Sealand evaluates the situation and remains hopeful they can resume in the future. When visits were available, reaching the platform required a boat from the UK mainland and then being hoisted 60 feet up on a manual crane-operated swing - one person at a time. E-citizenship subscribers receive priority access when trips do resume. Check [sealandgov.org](https://sealandgov.org) for the latest updates.

faqs.question: What is Sealand e-citizenship?
faqs.answer: Sealand e-citizenship is a $9.99/month subscription that provides digital membership of the principality. Benefits include a digital ID card (Apple/Google Wallet), a custom Sealand email address, VPN access, a 15% store discount, and priority access to future visits. It does not confer physical residency rights or affect your existing citizenship. The program launched in 2024, closed at end of 2024, and has since reopened; availability may vary. Confirm current status at [the e-citizenship page](https://sealandgov.org/en-us/pages/sealand-e-citizenship) before subscribing.

faqs.question: Does Sealand have sports teams?
faqs.answer: Sealand runs nine-plus national sports teams with 300+ registered athletes. The flagship is the Sealand Seahawks American football club, founded in summer 2021, which played its first official match in February 2022 and traveled to Las Vegas in December 2024 for a game against the MLFR Nationals. Other teams include the She-Hawks (women's football), cricket's Princes XI, basketball's Supersonics, softball's Seagulls, dodgeball's Slingers, and walking football squads. All competitive games are played off the platform, as the deck is too small for matches. Sealand also organizes an annual 12 km open water swim from the platform to the Suffolk coast, raising funds for [Aspire](https://www.aspire.org.uk/event/sealand-swim), a spinal injury charity.

faqs.question: Who governs Sealand?
faqs.answer: Sealand is a hereditary monarchy run by the Bates family. Sovereign Prince Michael Bates, son of founder Prince Roy, has led Sealand since his father's death in October 2012. His sons Prince James (Prince Royal, involved in day-to-day operations and representing Sealand at conferences) and Prince Liam (active in the Seahawks program), and daughter Princess Penny, are also involved. Mike Barrington, the platform's sole permanent resident, serves as engineer, caretaker, and head of homeland security.

faqs.question: Is a Sealand title legally recognized?
faqs.answer: Sealand titles are not recognized by any government or legal system outside Sealand itself. The official site acknowledges there are no formal legal privileges. That said, title-holders may style themselves with their title (Lord, Baroness, Duke, etc.) on personal correspondence and other documents where legal status is not required. Celebrity title-holders reportedly include Ed Sheeran and Jeremy Clarkson, per the official site.

faqs.question: Does Sealand have a passport?
faqs.answer: Sealand issued passports from 1975 until 1997, when the Bates family permanently revoked all of them after discovering a criminal ring had circulated approximately 150,000 fraudulent Sealand passports for money laundering and drug trafficking. No Sealand passports have been issued since. Physical passports are listed as a future feature on the e-citizenship page but are not currently available.

faqs.question: What happened during the 1978 Sealand coup?
faqs.answer: In August 1978, a German businessman named Alexander Achenbach hired mercenaries to seize Sealand while Prince Roy and Princess Joan were lured to Austria under false pretenses. The mercenaries overpowered Prince Michael, held him captive for four days, then transported him to the Netherlands. Prince Roy responded by launching a helicopter assault on August 16, retaking the platform at gunpoint. The German invaders were held as prisoners of war until Germany sent a diplomat from its London embassy to negotiate their release - an event the Bates family has since cited as evidence of de facto recognition.

faqs.question: What is the Sealand Open Water Swim?
faqs.answer: The Sealand Open Water Swim is an annual charity event in which participants swim 12 km from the Sealand platform to the Suffolk coast. Established in 2021, it has raised over £80,000 for [Aspire](https://www.aspire.org.uk/event/sealand-swim), a spinal injury charity. The swim is organized in partnership with Aspire; registration opens on their website.
